design.issue: A1: every request through a K-π Anthropic OAuth slot is refused with `400 {"type":"error","error":{"type":"invalid_request_error","message":"Claude Code 2.1.75 does not support this model; version 2.1.251 or newer is required. Run 'claude update', or update the Claude desktop app, then try again.","details":{"error_code":"claude_code_version_too_old"}},"request_id":"req_011CegQu2xW5e5oLygDDqtHQ"}` (verbatim errorMessage from ~/.kpi/agent/sessions/--Users-leebarry-K-pi--/2026-09-03T11-17-14-058Z_*.jsonl) because packages/ai still identifies as claude-cli/2.1.75, and K-π surfaces it only as the raw assistant error. A2: the official Anthropic grant lives in two files with two refreshers — the base runtime refreshes ~/.kpi/agent/auth.json on every request, K-π refreshes its accounts.secrets.json copy (anthropic/default) at every session_start/turn_start; Anthropic rotates refresh tokens, so the copy that refreshes second is dead forever (invalid_grant), the slot is cooled 5h instead of told to re-login, and the warning embeds a full JS stack every session start and every turn.
design.root_cause: A1: packages/ai/src/api/anthropic-messages.ts:77 pins `const claudeCodeVersion = "2.1.75"`, sent at :938 as `user-agent: claude-cli/<v>` (with `anthropic-beta: claude-code-20250219,oauth-2025-04-20` at :937) for every sk-ant-oat token (isOAuthToken :874-876). The server floor is now 2.1.251; upstream fixed it in 96317e50b (one line, 2.1.75 → 2.1.251, nothing else). In K-π the 400 reaches after_provider_response (index.ts:850) with no body, then message_end (:890) where classifyProviderBodyFailure (:930; QUOTA_TOKENS errors.ts:2) does not match the text, so the handler returns at :934 and says nothing. A2: one grant, two owners. (1) packages/coding-agent/src/core/model-runtime.ts:583 prepareRequest calls getAuth(model) on EVERY request before transformHeaders (:593) runs K-π's before_provider_headers hook; packages/ai/src/auth/resolve.ts:139-155 refreshes an auth.json OAuth credential with <5 min left under the auth.json lock and persists the rotated tokens. (2) store.ts:393-431 importOfficialCredentials copies auth.json's grant into accounts.secrets.json as slot `default` once (only when no `default`, :412); index.ts:559-585 refreshExpiringCredentials then calls oauth.refresh on that copy with the same refresh token. After either side rotates, the other side's refresh token is revoked (on this machine auth.json anthropic expires=1788453002792, the slot copy expires=1788387252486 — the base rotated, K-π's copy is dead). (3) index.ts:579 cools the slot DEFAULT_COOLDOWN_MS and :581 notifies error.message, which packages/ai/src/auth/oauth/anthropic.ts:330 builds from formatErrorDetails (:82-95, `stack=` at :92). (4) Every pooled OAuth login also lands in auth.json: index.ts:217 → model-runtime.ts:673-677 → packages/ai/src/models.ts:581 credentials.modify — so `/accounts login anthropic work` silently makes auth.json mirror `work` (two owners again). (5) When the base's own refresh dies, prepareRequest throws ModelsError("OAuth refresh failed for anthropic: …") whose message embeds the cause text via withCauseDetail (resolve.ts:30, :37-42), and packages/agent/src/agent.ts:511-524 turns it into an assistant error with that errorMessage; K-π's message_end has no pending response to pair (:898-899) and returns silently, so the operator is never told the grant in auth.json needs a new login.

event_or_data_contracts: accounts.json schema (version stays 1): AccountSlot gains `official?: true` — exactly one per pool at most, never on a `local` slot; the slot's grant is the one ~/.kpi/agent/auth.json holds, the base runtime is its only refresher, and it has NO accounts.secrets.json entry — and `needsLogin?: string` — a persisted reason; the slot is unselectable (balancer.selectInFamily) until `/accounts login <pool> <slot>` rewrites its credential (putSlot clears it).

AccountsStore API: `reconcileOfficialCredentials(now: number): Promise<{ imported: string[]; adopted: string[]; orphaned: string[] }>` replaces `importOfficialCredentials()` (removed, no alias); `readOfficialCredential(poolId): Promise<Credential | undefined>`; `claimOfficial(poolId, slotId, before: Credential | undefined): Promise<{ official: boolean; demoted?: string }>`; `markNeedsLogin(poolId, slotId, reason: string): Promise<void>`. K-π never writes auth.json; only the runtime's login does.

errors.ts exports: `parseClientVersionRejection(text: string | undefined): { sent?: string; required?: string } | undefined`; `type RefreshFailure = { kind: "invalid_grant" } | { kind: "http"; status: number; summary: string } | { kind: "transport"; summary: string }`; `summarizeRefreshFailure(error: unknown): RefreshFailure` (summary never contains `stack=` or a frame, <= 160 chars).

Assistant message diagnostic `kpi_client_version_rejected` with details `{ sent?: string; required?: string; slot?: "<pool>/<slot>" }`; it never triggers the agent-session retry (only `kpi_account_failover` does).

before_provider_headers contract: for a slot with `official: true` K-π leaves the runtime's auth header untouched (it is that slot's grant) and only records request attribution; non-official slots keep having their header set from accounts.secrets.json.

Exact notifications, each at most once per session per key: `K-π accounts: ${pool}/${slot} needs a new login: ${reason}. Run /accounts login ${pool} ${slot}` (error); `K-π ${VERSION} identifies to Anthropic as Claude Code ${sent}; Anthropic requires ${required} or newer for ${model}. Update K-π: npm install -g @korallis/k-pi@latest` (error, key `${sent}->${required}`); `K-π accounts: ${list} now reads its credential from auth.json` (info); `K-π accounts: could not refresh ${pool}/${slot}: ${summary}; cooling ${n}m` (warning); `K-π accounts: could not reconcile auth.json with accounts.json: ${message}` (error); `Added account ${pool}/${slot} (${pool}/${previous} keeps its previous grant)` (info) when a login demotes the previous official slot.
Widget: a slot with needsLogin renders `<label> <pct>%… needs login`.

Normative sync rule (docs/spec.md §13, pending NH-03): per pool at most one official slot; auth.json[pool] ≡ that slot's grant; it has no secrets entry; K-π never calls oauth.refresh on it; non-official slots exist only in accounts.secrets.json and are refreshed by K-π; a pooled OAuth login the runtime persisted into auth.json becomes the official slot and the previous official slot keeps the grant auth.json held until then as a K-π-refreshed secret; reconciliation runs once per session_start, by content match, then the `default`/expired-copy legacy rule, else a fresh official slot.

risks: Legacy stores carry no `official` flag; reconcile binds by content match, then binds `default` only when its secret is absent or an expired OAuth copy, else creates a fresh official slot (slot-2). A legacy `default` holding an alive access token from the same account but a rotated-away refresh token is therefore not bound; it later dies with invalid_grant and is named once as needing login (`/accounts login anthropic default`), and the operator may then `/accounts logout anthropic default`. Visible and bounded, never silent.

A legacy split where K-π's copy is the live lineage and auth.json's refresh token is the dead one is not repaired by publishing K-π's copy (K-π never writes auth.json): the base's refresh fails at prepareRequest, the official slot is marked needs-login once, and the pool is unavailable until `/accounts login anthropic <official>` — one command, then resend the prompt (no automatic retry; agent-session.ts:2880 retries only kpi_account_failover). Automatic promotion of a live sibling into auth.json was cut as an unrequested account substitution.

Transient refresh failures (network, 5xx, timeout) keep the existing 5-hour cooldown bound on non-official slots; only the wording changed. A successful refresh on a later turn_start does not clear that cooldown (existing behaviour, unchanged).

Base `/logout anthropic` mid-session removes auth.json's entry while the official slot stays selectable until the next session_start marks it orphaned; in between, prepareRequest fails with `Provider is not configured` (or the runtime's env fallback serves an env token). Existing exposure, now reported at the next session start.

`/accounts logout` of the official slot removes the slot but leaves auth.json's grant; the next session_start re-imports it as an official slot (`default` or next id) — existing re-import behaviour, unchanged.
reconcileOfficialCredentials runs inside session_start under try/catch; a malformed accounts.json still fails loudly there (assertAccounts), as today, and startup continues without a pool.
The cherry-pick lands one commit on this branch that upstream will also contain; the next upstream merge resolves it as already-applied. UPSTREAM.md records it.

open_questions: NH-03 (docs/remediation-plan.md): docs/PRD.md:190 AC-10.2 and docs/spec.md:649 say slot refresh is 'independent per slot, never by substituting the provider's current auth.json credential' / 'auth.json is not a substitute for slot refresh'. The base runtime refreshes auth.json on every request (model-runtime.ts:583, resolve.ts:139-155) and Anthropic rotates refresh tokens, so an official grant refreshed by both sides cannot stay valid. May the ACs be amended so the official slot's grant is auth.json's and the runtime is its only refresher (recommended; this design)? The only alternative that keeps the sentence literally true is patching the upstream file model-runtime.ts so prepareRequest skips getAuth for K-π pools — a larger upstream patch this design does not take.

problems.claim: An existing test encodes the opposite contract and would fail under the new reconcile rule, but the design neither changes nor removes it.
problems.evidence: test/accounts-commands.test.ts:276-292 `an existing default slot is never overwritten by the official import`: logs in `anthropic default` (harness login returns expires: 0, line 61), writes auth.json {access:"official", refresh:"r", expires:0}, runs session_start and asserts route() === "Bearer access-default" ("the operator's own slot wins"). Under reconcileOfficialCredentials: no `official` flag, no refresh/access match, fallback to slot `default`; secrets expires 0 is not later than auth.json expires 0, so the auth.json copy is adopted into secrets and credentialFor reads auth.json live → "Bearer official". `npm run test:kpi` fails as specified; the design's test list and docs edits do not mention this test or the sentence in docs/spec.md:649 it encodes.

problems.claim: The `OAuth refresh failed for <pool>` message_end path treats every base-runtime refresh failure as a dead grant, so a transient network/5xx/timeout during the base refresh marks the official slot needs-login and overwrites auth.json with a sibling's grant.
problems.evidence: packages/ai/src/auth/resolve.ts:150-153 wraps any oauth.refresh failure (including AbortSignal.timeout at :148-151, DNS errors, 503s from packages/ai/src/auth/oauth/anthropic.ts:184) as ModelsError("OAuth refresh failed for <provider>", {cause}); resolve.ts:30/37-42 withCauseDetail appends the cause message, so errorMessage is `OAuth refresh failed for anthropic: Anthropic token refresh request failed. url=…; details=…` for both invalid_grant and transport failures. The design's step (6) regexes only the prefix and unconditionally markNeedsLogin + promoteOfficial (writing the sibling's tokens into auth.json via AuthStorage.modify), displacing a still-valid official grant on a blip. summarizeRefreshFailure is available (the cause text with `status=`/`invalid_grant` is inside errorMessage) but is not applied here.

problems.claim: A pooled login can still orphan the previous official slot's grant: the runtime writes auth.json during `/accounts login` before K-π has adopted any rotation the base made since the last turn_start reconcile.
problems.evidence: packages/coding-agent/src/core/model-runtime.ts:583-591 refreshes auth.json on every request (mid-turn), K-π reconciles only on session_start/turn_start (design steps 7-8). loginAccount (accounts/index.ts:297) → context.modelRegistry.login → model-runtime.ts:673-677 → packages/ai/src/models.ts:581-589 credentials.modify replaces auth.json[pool] with the new slot's grant. claimOfficial then clears `official` from the previous slot, whose secrets copy still holds the pre-rotation refresh token (rotated away by the base during the turn) → K-π refreshes it later → invalid_grant → needs-login on a slot that was healthy. reconcileOfficialCredentials must run at the top of loginAccount before `login()`.

problems.claim: Legacy-store heuristic discards a live grant: when no slot content-matches auth.json, the design binds slot `default` and adopts the auth.json copy over `default`'s own secret even when that secret is a distinct, valid, K-π-refreshed grant.

The risks section admits the shared-grant outcome but not that the previous default grant is thrown away; prefer binding `default` only when its secret is missing/expired or shares lineage, otherwise import as a fresh official slot id.

problems.claim: The stated invariant 'one grant per slot' is not achieved by construction: the official slot keeps a second copy of the grant in accounts.secrets.json, a bidirectional reconcile (adopt/publish by later `expires`, or auth.json wins when kinds differ) runs on every session_start AND every turn_start, and credentialFor falls back to that copy. Since credentialFor reads auth.json live and K-π never refreshes the official slot, the per-turn reconcile and the secrets copy have no remaining purpose except as a fallback the design's own risk list says is unreachable (prepareRequest fails first with 'Provider is not configured'). This is a duplicate code path and a heuristic where a shape already in the store (a slot with no secrets entry, like `local` without `secretRef`) would make the invariant structural.

required_changes: Add open_questions for the two product decisions the design makes: (a) reversing AC-10.2/spec §13 so the base runtime owns and refreshes the official grant (raise NEEDS_HUMAN with both citations rather than rewriting the AC inside the fix); (b) whether K-π may rewrite auth.json with a sibling account's tokens when the official grant dies (promoteOfficial), and whether the runtime should spoof a Claude Code version learned from the server (KPI_CLAUDE_CODE_VERSION + adoption).
